extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, and typesetters preparing mathematical manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for presenting mathematical expressions, notation, punctuation, and manuscript marking so that mathematical copy is typeset, punctuated, and edited consistently and readably in publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma spacing after coordinate/list commas
rubrics_metrics.description: Commas used between coordinate points or in lists should be followed by a medium space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also rule 6.120; use medium space after commas in mathematical lists (and elided lists guidance in 12.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated mathematical functions spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviated functions are followed by a thin space unless the argument is enclosed in delimiters, in which case they are usually closed up to the opening delimiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In2n, sin(x+y), = min(x1, x2). Limits set as subscripts to the right in text and below in display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical expressions are part of sentence grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical expressions, whether run in with the text or displayed, are grammatically part of the surrounding sentence and must be edited for grammatical correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate several expressions in a single display with commas or semicolons; consecutive lines of a multiline expression should not be punctuated; expressions that end a sentence must carry ending punctuation aligned on the baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elided lists punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: In elided lists, commas should come after each term and after the ellipsis points if the list has a final term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: y = 0, 1, 2, ... not y = 0, 1, 2...5; use medium space after commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipsis position depends on separators
rubrics_metrics.description: Ellipsis points should be on the baseline when list terms are separated by commas; they should be vertically centered between operation or relation signs in elided sums or relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example baseline: 1,2,... ; example centered: x1 + x2 + ... + xn. If multiplication dot present, ellipsis on baseline; if multiplication cross present, ellipsis centered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juxtaposition implies multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplication is often signified by juxtaposition of factors without a multiplication sign (abc means a·b·c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When factors need separation use multiplication signs (dot or cross) or explicit sign; if dot is present then ellipsis baseline; if cross present then ellipsis centered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish multiplication dot and cross usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the multiplication dot or cross according to context; dot and cross may have different meanings (e.g., vectors) and are not interchangeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For numbers, choice may be preference; for vectors use appropriate symbol since meanings differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to display mathematical expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical expressions should be displayed (set on a separate line) if they are important to the exposition, referenced, or difficult to read/typeset inline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple expressions displayed on same line separate them by spacing, words, or punctuation. If displayed on separate consecutive lines, center alignment is usually acceptable, but alignment on relation signs can aid readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying clauses for displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying clauses may be displayed (separated by an em space), follow the displayed expression in text, precede it, or themselves include displayed expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown for each case; present qualifiers in the most readable position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking long displayed expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Long displayed expressions that do not fit on one line may be broken before a relation or operation sign; runover lines are aligned on relation signs which should be followed by thick spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a runover line begins with an operation sign, line it up with the first character to the right of the relation sign in the previous line, followed by a medium space. See table 12.1 for relation/operation signs list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation of displayed multiline groups
rubrics_metrics.description: If several expressions appear in a single display, separate them with commas or semicolons; but consecutive lines of a single multiline expression should not be punctuated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expressions that end a sentence need ending punctuation aligned on baseline even when preceded by subscripts/superscripts/fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering displayed equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical expressions referred to elsewhere should be numbered; all numbered expressions must be displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number enclosed in parentheses at right margin (or left margin rarely). In cross-references, enclose display numbers in parentheses to match marginal enumerations; range of numbers joined by an en dash (e.g., (2)-(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of numeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Display numbering may be single (reset each chapter) or double/triple (chapter.section.statement) for large works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double/triple numeration uses chapter first then section then number (1.1.1, 1.1.2...). For many numbered statements, consider numbering together in a single sequence apart from equations (e.g., definition 4.1, lemma 4.2...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimiters order and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Common delimiters are parentheses (), brackets [], and braces {}; their normal nested order is {[()]}. Angle brackets, vertical bars, and double vertical bars have special mathematical meaning and should not supplement this sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary extend with large delimiters; in text braces sometimes omitted from sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional notation grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: In functional notation, nested pairs of parentheses are used instead of brackets or braces to indicate grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (f∘g∘h)(x) = f(g(h(x))).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set notation - use braces
rubrics_metrics.description: Use braces {} to delimit elements of a set; do not substitute other delimiters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: {a1, a2, ..., an}. In set-builder notation use colon or vertical bar after the variable: {x : x ∈ D} or {x | x ∈ D}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordered tuple notation - parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use parentheses for ordered sets/tuples; do not substitute other delimiters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: (a, b) and (a1, a2, ..., an); parentheses indicate order (first element, second element).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interval notation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parentheses denote open intervals and brackets denote closed intervals; do not replace with other delimiters; alternative conventions may exist but preserve consistent author usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (a, b) open; [a, b] closed; (a, b] includes b not a. If author uses alternative form consistently (e.g., ]a,b[), do not change without instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimiters for inner product
rubrics_metrics.description: Parentheses are sometimes used to denote inner product (u, w); angle brackets are also used; do not interchange without consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 12.52–55 for related notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical bars meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical bars denote various special uses: modulus/absolute value |x|, vector length ||u|| (double vertical bar), cardinality |A|, or determinant |A| (context determines meaning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use notation appropriate to context; determinant also sometimes denoted det A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single vertical bar with limits (evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single vertical bar with limits is used to denote evaluation of a formula at a particular variable value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown with integral evaluation; format limits appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases formatting and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Displayed choices/cases may be grouped with a single brace and should be punctuated as clauses in ordinary language; alternatives can be long and then stated as separate equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuate each alternative as a clause. Examples provided for short and long alternatives; an alternative style (1 if x>0, 0 otherwise) is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscripts and superscripts conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-letter mathematical objects (Latin letters) are usually set in italics; abbreviations or words used in subscripts/superscripts are set in roman; maintain standard index positioning conventions (especially in tensor calculus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should query if authors deviate; specify italic for Latin single-letter math unless marked otherwise; stacking or staggering of indices permitted; do not change relative position of indices where conventions matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex subscripts/superscripts formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscripts/superscripts may themselves contain subscripts/superscripts or be built-out subformulas; align stacked or staggered as appropriate and preserve conventional index ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given; see 12.38 for index positioning discussion; use care in tensor notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summation/product/integral limits placement
rubrics_metrics.description: In text, limits for summation and product symbols are placed to the right of the symbol to avoid spreading lines; in display, limits are placed above and below the symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Σ_{i=1}^n in text as Σ_i=1^n to the right; display form uses upper/lower limits. For integrals, limits usually to the right in both text and display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral notation and differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Denote definite integrals with limits and dx as element of integration; place thin spaces before and after differentials; close up differential expressions in derivatives to the slash (dx/dt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: dV = r^2 sin θ dr dθ dφ. For functions of multiple variables use double integrals and name the region D: ∬_D f(x,y) dx dy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radical sign sizing and replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Radical sign extends vertically in display to fit radicand; in text use radical sign for simple radicands, otherwise prefer exponent notation with delimiters to avoid crowded lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example replace √(a^2 + b^2) with (a^2 + b^2)^{1/2} when complex or leading space is tight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractions in text and display
rubrics_metrics.description: Use slash for fractions in text (1/2); some common numerical fractions may be set as case fractions; in display, build up fractions with a horizontal bar unless part of numerator/denominator or in subscript/superscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enclose fractions in parentheses when followed by mathematical symbol: (a/b)x. For simple algebraic fractions in text prefer slash: (ax+b)/(cx+d) not inline stacked bar. Fractions in subscripts/superscripts always use slash. Fractions with summation/product/integral signs should be displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit fraction nesting and two-level preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer to limit fractions to two levels; if expression has more than one fraction display it and use a horizontal bar for principal fraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (a/b)+c vs (p/q)+r; continued fractions are displayed. Consider rewriting denominators as negative exponents to avoid deep nesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite complex denominators using exponents
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid nested fractions, represent denominators by using delimiters followed by exponent -1 or convert exponent to negative if already present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ab(cd)^{-1} instead of ab/(cd); change (cd)^2 in denominator to (cd)^{-2} when simplifying inline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrices presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrices are arrays displayed in rectangular rows and columns, enclosed with large brackets or parentheses; row and column matrices may be represented inline for small sizes but most matrices are displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using matrix notation for multiline equations; inline matrices cannot be broken; display matrices cannot be broken across columns/pages. Examples for row/column vectors and transpose notation provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant notation
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is square, denote determinant by |A| or det A; vertical bars distinguish determinant from matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jacobian matrix and determinant examples provided; choose notation consistent with context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalars, vectors, tensors notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scalars typically lowercase italic/Greek; vectors often boldface or with arrow diacritic; tensors are multidimensional and extend vector concept; a scalar is tensor rank 0 and vector rank 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because authors may not follow conventions, editors should query; unit vectors denoted with circumflex; vector expressed as sum of components with index notation examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector/tensor multiplication notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Dot product denoted u·w (boldface dot); cross product u×w (boldface cross); tensor product T ⊗ S; index notation and Einstein summation convention may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interchange dot and cross; index positioning (raising/lowering) must be preserved; examples and Einstein summation explanation given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional tensor derivative notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use comma subscript for ordinary derivative (A_{,i}) and semicolon subscript for covariant derivative (A_{;i}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related index positioning rules in 12.38.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dirac bracket notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Dirac bra–ket notation used in physics: ⟨a|b⟩, ⟨a|T|b⟩, with ⟨a| and |b⟩ denoting dual vectors and vectors respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious that (a|T|b) ≠ (a T b) and combinations used with operators must be typeset clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting enunciations (theorem/definition/etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads of definitions, theorems, propositions, corollaries, lemmas, axioms, and rules (enunciations) should be distinguished from body text—commonly caps and small caps, bold, or italic—and their numbers are not enclosed in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In definitions italicize the term being defined. Cross-reference numbers for enunciations are not enclosed in parentheses. Proofs often end with QED or a symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting for math (paper copy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical manuscripts should be printed one-sided, double-spaced, on 8.5 x 11-inch white paper with 1.5-inch text margins and 2-inch display margins; high print quality (300 dpi) and generous space for handwritten insertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ample margins so editor can instruct typesetter; mark unusual characters that typesetter might not reproduce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking italic type for mathematics on paper manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor should either underline all copy to be set in italics or give general instruction to typesetter to set all Latin single-letter mathematical objects in italics unless marked otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General instruction should also specify italics for letters in subscripts/superscripts; if author already used italics, instruct typesetter to follow copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking mathematical abbreviations and roman letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations for common functions, points, units, and elements (set in roman) should be marked as roman by the editor only where ambiguity could occur; use marking for letters that must be in roman rather than italic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See table 12.2 for common abbreviations; underline conventions: single underline = italics, double underline = small caps, wavy underline = boldface; color codes may be used but avoid color if photocopying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking special mathematical typefaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Boldface, script, Fraktur, sans serif, and double-struck (blackboard) characters must be clearly indicated on paper manuscripts using underlining, color codes, or other marking conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (ABCD in different faces); double-struck often used for N, Z, Q, R, C; color coding must be explained to typesetter and avoid color when photocopying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking subscripts and superscripts for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: If inferior/superior characters are ambiguous, mark them (e.g., with symbols v and Λ) or give clear examples to show intended stacking/staggering and alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples to disambiguate whether X^k, X_k, X^{k}, etc.; mark stacked or staggered indices where needed to avoid typesetter confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure legible handwriting and identify ambiguous symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegible handwriting and unidentifiable signs reduce composition speed and cause costly corrections; identify ambiguous symbols and provide marginal notations or a list of symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 12.4 lists commonly ambiguous symbols and suggested marginal notation; give clarifying remarks (e.g., leave medium space before/after binary operation signs; avoid using slash/other substitutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing around binary operation signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave a medium space before and after binary operation signs (=, <, ∈, ∧, etc.), but do not add space when such signs are used to modify symbols or expressions (-3, +1) or when operations appear as subscripts/superscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically advise spacing for multiplication '×' and dot, and caution about not adding space in chemical formulas or negative quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript symbol marginal notation and remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply marginal notations for ambiguous characters with recommended verbal labels (e.g., 'alpha' for α, 'ell' for l) and note special handling items (avoid using @ for / if / is available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 12.4 provides a large mapping of symbols, marginal notation examples, and remarks for manuscript preparation.
